heart.intro.welcome.title: Where things are
heart.intro.welcome.body:
The sheets roll, mark, and remind for you, so the rules stay out of the way. The next two pages are the rules themselves.

Players

  • Your character. Choose your ancestry, calling, and class from the empty slots in your sheet's header: each opens cards from the books.
  • Rolling. Press Roll in the header, or click a skill or domain. The prompt shows your dice before you roll. When the GM asks for a roll it arrives in chat: press Roll on the card.
  • Stress. When a roll costs you, press Roll Stress on its card. The stress card that follows shows what you would take; anything that changes it (an ability, a guard) happens now, then Take Stress marks it on your sheet. Then Roll Fallout: you or the GM roll the check, and the GM picks any fallout.
  • Bonds and the party. Your bonds (up to three) are on the Character tab. The party sheet holds the shared Provisions, the party's items and companions, pursued beats, and a board of notes anyone can add to.
  • Your look. The Art and Glass buttons in a sheet's title bar turn the books' art and the glass look on and off, just for you. Configure Settings has the colour scheme and the glass sliders.

GMs

  • Request Roll and Pursued Beats are at the top of the Actors sidebar.
  • Fallout cards carry a Pick Fallout button only you see.
  • Create Board in the Scenes sidebar starts the party's map.
  • Landmarks, adversaries, companions, and the rest come from the Heart content module's compendiums.
heart.intro.rolling.title: The rules: rolling
heart.intro.rolling.body:
Play is a conversation: the GM describes the world, you say what you do, and the GM says what happens. Most of it needs no dice. You roll when something is at stake: the action is risky, dangerous, or matters.

Build your pool

Every roll is a handful of d10s:

  • one die for the action itself;
  • one more if a skill fits (what you do);
  • one more if a domain fits (where you are, what you know);
  • one for mastery, from a knack or an ability, never more than one;
  • one for each helper, two at most (another delver in the party, or a bonded companion whose ability gives assistance), who risks the same stress you do.

Difficulty

The GM says how hard it is before you roll, and you can always back out. Risky removes your highest die after the roll, Dangerous your two highest. If that leaves no dice, roll one d10: a 10 is a success at a cost, anything else a failure. An Impossible action isn't rolled: it fails, and you take stress anyway.

Read the highest die

  • 10: critical success. It works, and any stress you deal steps up a die size.
  • 8 or 9: success.
  • 6 or 7: success, but you take stress.
  • 2 to 5: failure, and you take stress.
  • 1: critical failure, and double stress.

When you are only trying to avoid harm, a 6 or 7 costs one die size less. The roll card does the counting and offers the stress afterwards.
heart.intro.stress.title: The rules: stress and fallout
heart.intro.stress.body:
You have five resistances, each a track of twelve boxes (Stress past the last box still counts, shown as +N): Blood (injury and exhaustion), Mind (madness and the uncanny), Echo (the Heart changing you), Fortune (bad luck and unwanted attention), and Supplies (gear, money, and debt; the party's food, water, and light are its shared Provisions).

Marking stress

The GM names a resistance and a die: a d4 near the surface, larger deeper down. Roll it, subtract your Protection on that resistance (the shields beside its track), and mark the rest. Stress does nothing on its own, and it stays until something clears it.

Fallout

Every time you mark stress, you or the GM roll a d12 (Roll Fallout on the stress card) against your total stress across all five tracks. Higher, and you are fine. Equal or lower: on a 1 to 6 you take Minor fallout and clear that resistance; on a 7 to 12, Major fallout, and you clear every track. The GM picks which fallout; you can lobby. Fallout is the real harm: a wound, a fear, a curse, a debt.

Two Minors can combine into a Major, and two Majors into a Critical fallout, which ends your character's story. Haunts (paid with a resource), healing, some abilities, and time at a haven clear stress; a haunt can treat fallout too.

Growing

Your calling gives you beats, goals you pursue two at a time. Completing them earns advances: new abilities from your class and calling.

heart.party-sheet.restock-desc: In a haven or with a merchant: the payer takes D4, D6, or D8 Supplies Stress, and Provisions Stress is reduced by one die size larger.
heart.party-sheet.scavenge-desc: A successful Delve+Domain scavenge in the field.
heart.party-sheet.relieve-desc: A haunt that treats Supplies, a sold resource, or mended Supplies gear.
heart.party-sheet.clear-desc: After a Provisions Fallout, or a few days resting in Derelictus.
heart.party-sheet.amount-tip: A fixed amount instead of the die
heart.party-sheet.fallout-hint: None. Drop Provisions fallouts here; they befall every delver.
heart.party-sheet.name: Name
heart.party-sheet.no-candidates: Every character is already in the party.
heart.party-sheet.no-members: No members yet. Drag characters onto this sheet from the Actors directory, or use +.
heart.party-sheet.not-owner: You don't own the party, so its controls are hidden.
heart.party-sheet.note-delete: Take this note off the board
heart.party-sheet.note-delete-confirm: Take "{title}" off the board? It can't be brought back.
heart.party-sheet.board-empty: No notes yet. Use + to pin one to the board.
heart.party-sheet.only-characters: Only characters can join the party.
heart.party-sheet.only-fallout: Only Fallout, equipment, resources, and items can be added to the party.
heart.party-sheet.own-only: You can add or remove only your own characters. The GM can change anyone.
heart.party-sheet.protection-none: No quartermaster: Provisions has no Protection.
heart.party-sheet.protection-tip: Protection {count}: the quartermaster {name}'s Supplies Protection (0 under the Empty Fallout).
heart.party-sheet.quartermaster-tip: Quartermaster: their Supplies Protection applies to Stress marked to Provisions; change it between scenes.
heart.party-sheet.reset-confirm: Fully reset {name} for a new adventure? Its name and portrait go back to the defaults, every member leaves, the quartermaster is dropped, Provisions goes to 0, and every party Fallout, every party item, and the notes are deleted. Characters keep their own sheets and gear.
heart.party-sheet.reset-tip: Start a new adventure: clears the party's members, quartermaster, Provisions, Fallout, items, and notes.
heart.party-sheet.items-hint: None. Drop equipment, resources, or items here to share them, or use +.
heart.party-sheet.status-dire: Past {past}: every check is Fallout, and a Major result is Critical.
heart.party-sheet.status-full: Provisions are full: no roll, the Fallout is Critical.
heart.party-sheet.track-tip: Provisions {value} of {max}. From {critical}, every check is Fallout and a Major result is Critical; at {max}, the Fallout is Critical with no roll.
heart.roll-prompt.companion-assists: Assists through {ability}: {trigger} If that applies to this roll, it adds a D10 and takes the same Stress.
heart.roll-prompt.companion-assists-note: Assists (from its notes): {trigger} If that applies to this roll, it adds a D10 and takes the same Stress.
heart.roll-prompt.companion-despondent: {name} is Despondent: pass a Compel check before it assists.
heart.roll-prompt.companion-many: {name} helps several characters at once: it takes Stress once, from the worst result.
heart.roll-prompt.companion-no-assistanc: Has no ability that gives assistance. A companion has no skills or domains, so it helps only through one.
heart.roll-prompt.companion-overambitiou: {name} is Overambitious: if its demand was ignored, it has lost its ability until that Fallout is resolved.
heart.roll-prompt.companions-hint: A companion helps only when its ability applies; you decide. It counts toward the two helpers, adds a D10, and takes the same Stress.
heart.roll-prompt.companions-why: only through an ability that gives assistance
heart.roll-prompt.difficulty-tip.dangero: Dangerous: remove the two highest dice before reading the result. With no dice left, roll one D10 on the Difficult Actions table.
heart.roll-prompt.difficulty-tip.impossi: Impossible: no roll; the action fails and you take Stress.
heart.roll-prompt.difficulty-tip.risky: Risky: remove the highest die before reading the result. With no dice left, roll one D10 on the Difficult Actions table.
heart.roll-prompt.difficulty-tip.standar: Standard: roll the pool and read the highest die.
heart.roll-prompt.difficulty-why: set by the GM when the stakes are stated
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.battered: Battered: offensive combat actions are Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.blinded: Blinded: anything that needs sight is Dangerous.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.broken-ar: Broken Arm: actions with that arm are Risky, Dangerous, or Impossible.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.broken-le: Broken Leg: actions that need the leg fail.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.darkness: Darkness: Delve and Discern actions are Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.limping: Limping: fast or stealthy movement is Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.no-ration: No Rations: all actions are Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.ringing-h: Ringing Head: the next action is Dangerous, then Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.siren-son: Siren Song: anything but following the song is Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.fallout-hint.spitting-: Spitting Teeth: speaking or looking respectable is Risky.
heart.roll-prompt.gm-override: As GM you can pick anyone.
heart.roll-prompt.helper-full: Two helpers already: the most a roll can have
heart.roll-prompt.helper-furious: Furious: can't add a die to anyone's roll.
heart.roll-prompt.helper-has: Has {what}: adds a D10 and takes the same Stress.
heart.roll-prompt.helper-lacks: Has neither the skill nor the domain
heart.roll-prompt.helper-pick-first: Pick a skill or domain first
heart.roll-prompt.helpers-why: each adds a die and takes the same stress
heart.roll-prompt.knack-applies: Roll with mastery if it applies to this action.
heart.roll-prompt.mastery-sources: From a knack that applies, a class ability, Renowned gear, or a GM award for good preparation.
heart.roll-prompt.say-cut-1: Remove the highest die, keep the best of the other {left}.
heart.roll-prompt.say-cut-2: Remove the two highest dice, keep the best of the other {left}.
heart.roll-prompt.say-fresh: {difficulty} removes all {count}, so roll one fresh d10 on the Difficult table.
heart.roll-prompt.say-impossible: The action fails and you take stress. Do it anyway for the story or as a distraction.
heart.roll-prompt.title: Roll
heart.rolls.fallout-roll.confirm-major: {name} took Major fallout. Clear the stress in every resistance ({count} boxes marked)?
heart.rolls.fallout-roll.confirm-minor: {name} took Minor fallout. Clear the stress in {resistance} ({count} boxes marked)?
heart.rolls.fallout-roll.not-rolled: Provisions are full. No roll: the fallout is Critical.
heart.rolls.roll.crit-step-up: Critical success: step up the stress you inflict.
heart.rolls.roll.summary-fresh: {difficulty} removed every die: one fresh d10 on the Difficult table
heart.rolls.roll.summary-impossible: Impossible: no roll, the action fails
heart.rolls.stress-roll.blocked: {name}: Protection stops it all. No fallout.
heart.rolls.stress-roll.die-hint: Default D4 on Tiers 0-1, unless the landmark or delve says otherwise.
heart.rolls.stress-roll.no-resistance: Pick a resistance for this stress first.
heart.rolls.stress-roll.passive-hint: A passive action that succeeds at a cost takes stress one die size smaller.
heart.rolls.stress-roll.takes: {name} takes {amount} {resistance} stress (mark it on their sheet).
heart.tip.skill.compel: Compel: make people do what you want via threats, lies, flattery, or reasoned argument.
heart.tip.skill.delve: Delve: progress into dangerous or unknown territory.
heart.tip.skill.discern: Discern: understand the world by drawing on accessible information.
heart.tip.skill.endure: Endure: resist the effects of the Heart on your body and mind.
heart.tip.skill.evade: Evade: get away from someone or something that's trying to track you down.
heart.tip.skill.hunt: Hunt: track down someone or something that's trying to get away from you.
heart.tip.skill.kill: Kill: end the lives of people and things, with weapons or your bare hands.
heart.tip.skill.mend: Mend: repair something or someone that is broken, or build something new.
heart.tip.skill.sneak: Sneak: hide yourself or things from the attention of others.
heart.tip.domain.cursed: Cursed: actively harmful locations, places touched by the Heart.
heart.tip.domain.haven: Haven: settlements where people live, work, and form communities.
heart.tip.domain.occult: Occult: hidden knowledge and black magic.
heart.tip.domain.religion: Religion: gods, and things worshipped like gods.
heart.tip.resistance.blood: Blood: physical exhaustion, pain, blood loss, and injury.
heart.tip.resistance.echo: Echo: the twisting of body and mind by the Heart's unreal energies.
heart.tip.resistance.fortune: Fortune: bad luck, incompetence, and overconfidence.
heart.tip.resistance.bond: Bond: Fallout that lands on a bond, a hireling, or an animal, not on you.
heart.tip.resistance.supplies: Supplies: loss of resources, damaged equipment, and debt.
heart.tip.resistance.provisions: Provisions: the whole party's food, water, light, and medicine, on one shared track. Its Fallout befalls every delver.
heart.tip.beats-limit: Two beats are active at a time, and you can hit only one per situation.
heart.tip.beat.pursue: Pursue: you choose your two active beats at the end of each session.
heart.tip.beat.finish: Finish: hitting a beat earns an advance of its level; each beat counts only once.
heart.tip.equipment.kill: Kill: roll this die to inflict Stress on an adversary; without a weapon, it is D4.
heart.tip.equipment.delve: Delve: roll this die to inflict Stress on a delve; without such gear, it is D4.
heart.tip.equipment.mend: Mend: roll this die to remove Stress.
heart.tip.equipment.miscellaneous: Miscellaneous: usually a story effect rather than a Stress die.
heart.tip.haunt.service: Pay a resource to remove its rolled value in Stress here, up to this die size.
heart.tip.haunt.track: Upgrade track: mark it each use; paying the full price without removing Stress marks three.
heart.tip.haunt.upgrade: Upgrade: at six marks, clear them and step up the haunt's dice, from the next visit.
heart.tip.haunt.downgrade: Downgrade: step the haunt's dice down; a D4 haunt that is downgraded is gone.
heart.tip.adversary.difficulty: Difficulty: Standard rolls as normal, Risky removes the highest die, and Dangerous the two highest.
heart.tip.adversary.resistance: Resistance: what it has left. Stress inflicted on it marks boxes and comes off what is left; at 0 left, it is at your mercy.
heart.tip.adversary.protection: Protection: subtract it from all incoming Stress.
heart.tip.delve.resistance: Resistance: a success or partial success inflicts Stress on it, D4 by default; at 0, the journey is complete.
heart.tip.landmark.stress: Default Stress: the standard Stress a delver here takes on a failure or partial success.
heart.tip.party.upkeep: Upkeep: D4 Stress to Provisions, less the quartermaster's Protection.
heart.tip.party.use: Use Provisions: mark Stress here instead of Supplies when the whole party pays the price.
heart.tip.party.volunteer: Become the quartermaster: your Supplies Protection protects Provisions. You can resign it later.
heart.tip.party.resign: Stop being the quartermaster: Provisions has no Protection until someone volunteers or the GM picks one.
heart.tip.party.restock: Restock: mark D4, D6, or D8 to your own Supplies to remove one die size larger from Provisions. Ending a Provisions Fallout is a separate payment: D6 for a Minor, D8 for a Major.
heart.tip.party.scavenge: Scavenge: roll Delve+Domain; a success or a success at a cost removes D4, and a failure finds nothing.
heart.tip.party.relieve: Relieve: only restocking, scavenging, Supplies haunts, sold resources, and Mend Supplies equipment remove Provisions Stress.
heart.tip.party.clear: Clear: a Provisions Fallout of any severity clears the track, and so do a few days in Derelictus.
heart.tip.ignore-protection: Ignore Protection: mark the full roll, as when Piercing or a Fallout such as Shattered turns Protection off.
heart.tip.stakes.passive: Passive: rolling only to avoid harm; on a 6-7, the Stress is one die size lower.
heart.tip.stakes.d4: D4: the lowest Stress, and the usual die on Tiers 0 and 1.
heart.tip.stakes.d6: D6: the usual die on Tiers 2 and 3.
heart.tip.stakes.d8: D8: the usual die on Tier 4.
heart.tip.stakes.d12: D12: the highest Stress a situation can inflict.
heart.tip.card.take-stress: Mark this Stress on the roller and every helper, less each one's Protection.
heart.tip.card.roll-stress: Roll the Stress die the GM names. Nothing is marked yet: the stress card's Take Stress marks it on the roller and every helper, less their own Protection.
heart.tip.card.stress-pending: Nothing is marked until the GM or the roller's player presses Take Stress. Apply anything that changes it first, by hand: an ability that adds Protection, a guard, or a redirect.
heart.tip.card.request-stakes: The GM's stakes for this roll. Roll Stress starts from them; whoever rolls the stress can still change them.
heart.tip.card.party-fallout: Provisions Fallout: a D12 against Provisions alone, and it befalls every delver. From 13 Stress, every check is Fallout and Major is Critical.
heart.tip.card.clear-provisions: A Provisions Fallout of any severity clears the track.
heart.tip.tag-uses: Limited X: the uses before it gives out; -1 is unlimited.
heart.term.stress: Stress: marked to a resistance on a failure or a success at a cost. Each time, a Fallout check follows.
heart.term.protection: Protection: reduce Stress taken by this much; if none gets through, there is no Fallout roll.
heart.term.fallout: Fallout: each time you mark Stress, you or the GM roll a D12 (Roll Fallout); equal to or under your total Stress is Minor (1-6) or Major (7-12), and the GM picks which Fallout.
heart.term.minor-fallout: Minor Fallout: clear all Stress in its resistance. Two Minors can combine into a Major.
heart.term.major-fallout: Major Fallout: clear all Stress in every resistance. Two Majors can combine into a Critical.
heart.term.critical-fallout: Critical Fallout: the end of the character, by death, madness, or another ignoble end.
heart.term.mastery: Mastery: one extra D10, only once per roll however many sources you have.
heart.term.knack: Knack: a Skill or Domain gained a second time, narrowed to one facet; when it applies, roll with Mastery.
heart.term.skill: Skill: what you do; having the Skill that fits adds a D10.
heart.term.domain: Domain: an area of the Heart, knowledge, or connections; having the Domain that fits adds a D10.
heart.term.resistance: Resistance: a delver's Stress track (Blood, Mind, Echo, Fortune, or Supplies); on an adversary or delve, the Stress it takes to finish it.
heart.term.roll: Skill+Domain: roll a D10, plus one for the Skill and one for the Domain if you have them, and read the highest.
heart.term.dangerous: Dangerous: as a difficulty, remove the two highest dice. As a tag, the item's maximum roll marks D6 Stress to Blood.
heart.term.tag.awkward: Awkward: the resource is heavy or hard to carry.
heart.term.tag.beacon: Beacon: the resource attracts something dangerous towards its position.
heart.term.tag.bloodbound: Bloodbound: mark D4 Stress to Blood to roll with Mastery using this for the rest of the situation.
heart.term.tag.brutal: Brutal: when you roll Stress against an adversary with this, roll two dice and keep the highest; each extra Brutal adds a die.
heart.term.tag.conduit: Conduit: mark D4 Stress to Mind to roll with Mastery using this for the rest of the situation.
heart.term.tag.dangerous: Dangerous: when this item's die rolls its maximum, mark D6 Stress to Blood.
heart.term.tag.debilitating: Debilitating: once per situation, after you inflict Stress with this, the next attack against those targets rolls with Mastery.
heart.term.tag.degenerating: Degenerating: if it hurt you, roll Endure+Domain at the end of the situation; a failure marks D6 Stress, a partial success D4.
heart.term.tag.deteriorating: Deteriorating: the resource is breaking down; get it to a new owner quickly.
heart.term.tag.distressing: Distressing: when this item's die rolls its maximum, mark D6 Stress to Mind.
heart.term.tag.double_barreled: Double-Barreled: as Reload, but it can be used twice before reloading.
heart.term.tag.expensive: Expensive: when this item's die rolls its maximum, mark D6 Stress to Supplies.
heart.term.tag.extreme_range: Extreme Range: it can be used at extreme range.
heart.term.tag.fragile: Fragile: the resource is destroyed if dropped or damaged.
heart.term.tag.harmful: Harmful: the resource can harm whoever carries it, by black magic, illness, or strange energies.
heart.term.tag.limited: Limited X: it can be used X times before it gives out.
heart.term.tag.loud: Loud: when this item's die rolls its maximum, mark D6 Stress to Fortune.
heart.term.tag.mobile: Mobile: left unattended, the resource leaves of its own accord.
heart.term.tag.niche: Niche: the resource is only valuable to a very select group of people.
heart.term.tag.obscuring: Obscuring: the bearer and nearby allies reduce incoming and outgoing ranged damage by one step.
heart.term.tag.one_shot: One-Shot: it can only be used once per situation.
heart.term.tag.piercing: Piercing: Blood Protection cannot reduce its Stress, and adversaries get no Protection against it.
heart.term.tag.point_blank: Point-Blank: as Ranged; at very close range its Stress die steps up, and far enough to spread out, it steps down.
heart.term.tag.potent: Potent: when you roll Stress removed with this, roll two dice and keep the highest; it stacks like Brutal.
heart.term.tag.ranged: Ranged: it can be used at range.
heart.term.tag.rare: Rare: finding a trader can take a Discern+Haven roll; every Excellent item is rare.
heart.term.tag.reload: Reload: it must be reloaded between uses, giving enemies a chance to close in or flee.
heart.term.tag.smoke: Smoke: as Obscuring, but only when used, and only around where it was used.
heart.term.tag.spread: Spread: on a success, anyone near the target rolls Evade+Domain to avoid the Stress too; a partial success steps it down.
heart.term.tag.taboo: Taboo: most haunts won't take the resource in barter.
heart.term.tag.tiring: Tiring: when you fail an action with it, its Stress die steps down for the rest of the situation.
heart.term.tag.trusty: Trusty: when you roll Stress against a delve with it, roll two dice and keep the highest; it stacks like Brutal.
heart.term.tag.unreliable: Unreliable: when you fail an action with it, it can't be used for the rest of the situation, or of the journey on a delve.
heart.term.tag.volatile: Volatile: the resource may explode if mistreated.
heart.term.tag.wyrd: Wyrd: when this item's die rolls its maximum, mark D6 Stress to Echo.
heart.trinket.pick-lead: The {table} table: pick one instead of rolling.
heart.trinket.no-table: No table found for {name}. Import the trinket and keepsake tables, or create a table named "{name} Keepsakes" or "{name} Calling Trinkets".
heart.warn.party: Not in a party yet. Drag the party from the Actors sidebar onto this sheet.
heart.warn.keepsake: Keepsakes not all drawn yet: roll or pick two.
heart.warn.no-quartermaster: No quartermaster yet: Provisions has no Protection. A player can volunteer their own character, or the GM picks one on the party sheet.
heart.glass.reset-done: The GM set the glass sliders (see-through, blur, and tint) back to their defaults. You can change them again in Configure Settings.
heart.board.help.inspect:
Look is only for looking. Nothing on the board changes when Look is in hand. When you take Look, the selection is let go.

- **Point** at a note, writing, a string, or a stroke to see whose it is.
- **Click** a place to open it.
- **Click and hold** to ping that spot for everyone.
- **Click the tool in hand again** to come back to Look.
heart.board.locked-frozen: That is locked. Right-click it with Move to let it go first.
heart.board.doodle-wheel: Ctrl+wheel turns the doodle in hand, Shift+wheel sizes it.
heart.board.doodle-save-hint: Select strokes with Move, then keep them here as a doodle of your own, on every map.
heart.board.doodle-save-none: Pick strokes first, or select them with Move.
heart.board.doodle-save-full: You have {n} doodles of your own. Forget one first (right-click it).
heart.board.doodles-yours-empty: Your own doodles land here: pick strokes on the board, then Save.
heart.board.doodle-yours-hint: Your own drawing, in its own paints. Right-click to forget it.
heart.board.doodle-forget-confirm: Forget this drawing of yours? Anything you already laid with it stays on the board.
heart.board.hand-free-confirm: Free {hand} from {who}? They pick a hand again the next time they write. Their notes already on the board keep the hand they were written in.
heart.board.create-hint: A new scene with a board on it, in the style you choose. The Board tab of the scene's settings changes its style, background, and size later.
heart.board.style-hint: The whole look: the sheet, its light and grime, and the cards' papers, pins, strings, and paints.
heart.board.tab-hint: This scene's board: its style, its background, and its size. Saved with Save Changes.
heart.board.tab-bg-hint: The scene's own keeps its picture, size, and grid, with the board's cards, strings, and drawing over them. A baked map is a map painted once into tiles (the Village of Plenty's, say), with the board over it.
heart.board.tab-baked-hint: The manifest.json the bake wrote, in the content module's boards folder.
heart.board.tab-baked-square-hint: How much of the map one 50 px square holds; a person's token is one square. Saving makes the scene the map's size at that square, with token vision and fog exploration off. Map layers switches between feet and metres any time.
heart.board.square-5ft: 5 ft (the tabletop standard), measured in feet
heart.board.tab-pages-hint: The sheet's size in pages. Pages come and go on its right and bottom; File, Sheet adds them on any side.
heart.board.tab-page-hint: How big each page is: the paper's tiling. Empty: the style's own, {w} x {h}.
heart.board.tab-size-scene: The board: the scene's own size.
heart.board.tab-size-baked: The board: the baked map's size, at the square above.
heart.board.tab-refused: The sheet would cut through what is on the board. It needs at least {w} x {h} px.
heart.board.sheet-bare: This board is on its scene's own background: the scene's settings (Grid) set its size.
heart.board.unmake-ask: Take the board off {scene}? Its board ({cards} cards, {strings} strings) is deleted from the scene. A copy is kept in this browser's File, Earlier boards, and Make a Board then Put back brings it back.
heart.board.converted: {name} is now a board: its places and strings are on the new map.
heart.board.gm-only: Only the GM can change the map.
heart.board.no-look: The map's look (fvtt-heart-content heart-board.json) is missing: the board is blank paper.
heart.board.placed: {name} is pinned to the map, hidden. Reveal it when the delvers find it.
heart.board.place-made: {name} is pinned to the map, known to the delvers.
heart.board.place-hint: A place of your own, made at the table: a landmark actor in the Board places folder, its card on the board. Fill in its sheet whenever you like; its card follows its name.
heart.board.place-no-name: A new place needs a name.
heart.board.place-click-now: Click the board where {name} goes (Escape lets it go).
heart.board.place-gone: The place behind {name} is gone: its actor was deleted.
heart.board.reshuffle-none: Select a place or a note to reshuffle how it's put together.
heart.board.key-reshuffle: Board: reshuffle the selected cards (the GM's)
heart.board.tool.sheet: Sheet size: pages on any side
heart.board.sheet-hint: Add pages on any side of the sheet, or take them away. New pages are made like the rest; everything on the board keeps its place on its paper. Pages with anything on them can't be taken away.
heart.board.sheet-refused: Something on the board lies on the pages at the {side}: move it first.
heart.board.not-yours-tied: Someone else's strings or pins go with that card, so only the GM can take it off.
heart.board.erase-scrap-player: Delete {name}? The GM keeps it in Removed cards, and Ctrl+Z puts it back.
heart.board.erase-cards-player: Delete these {n} notes and writing? The GM keeps them in Removed cards, and Ctrl+Z puts them back.
heart.board.undo-forgotten: The GM's client has reloaded since those edits, so they can't be undone or redone now. Your edits from here on can.
heart.board.undo-failed: That couldn't be undone or redone just now. It is kept, so try again. The console (F12) has the details.
heart.board.key-redo: Board: redo your last undone edit
heart.board.bin-hint: Cards taken off this board, newest first. Put one back and it returns where it was, with its pins and the strings whose other ends are still there.
heart.board.bin-none: Nothing has been taken off this board.
heart.board.bin-empty-confirm: Let go of all {n} removed cards for good? They can't be put back after this.
heart.board.history-hint: Copies of this board kept by this browser: when the session started, every few minutes while it's edited, and just before cards come off or the board is replaced. Putting one back replaces the board; Undo takes that back.
heart.board.history-none: No copies of this board yet in this browser.
heart.board.history-confirm: Replace the board with this copy? Undo takes it back, and the board you have now is kept as a copy too.
heart.board.history-done: The earlier board is back. Ctrl+Z takes it back again.
heart.board.brush-reset-confirm: Rub out every brush stroke on this board, on the sheet and on the cards, everyone's? Ctrl+Z takes it back.
heart.board.brush-dim-hint: Darker: the paint mixed toward black.
heart.board.brush-bright-hint: Lighter: the paint mixed toward white.
heart.board.face-sample: We went down past the Grip
heart.board.erase-cards: Delete these {n} cards, with their pins and strings? They go to File: Removed cards, and Ctrl+Z puts them back.
heart.board.note-turn-left: Turn the paper a quarter left.
heart.board.note-turn-right: Turn the paper a quarter right.
heart.board.no-backup: There is no backup board yet (an import keeps the board it replaces).
heart.board.import-confirm: Replace the whole board of {scene} with the file's? The board there now is kept as the backup board (Swap in the backup board) and in File, Earlier boards.
heart.board.bin-full: The bin was full, so its oldest removed cards ({n}) were let go. A copy of the board from just before is in File, Earlier boards.
heart.board.download-remind: {scene} was last downloaded {days} days ago. File, Download the board keeps a copy of your own.
heart.board.download-never: {scene} has not been downloaded on this computer yet. File, Download the board keeps a copy of your own.
heart.board.strings-deleted: Strings and pins deleted ({n}). Ctrl+Z puts them back.
heart.board.restore-confirm: Swap this board for the backup? (The current one becomes the backup.)
heart.board.erase-scrap: Delete {name}, with its pins and the strings tied to it? It goes to File: Removed cards, and Ctrl+Z puts it back.
heart.board.string-name-hint: Blank: none (a name hangs on it as a tag)
heart.board.note-enter: Enter writes it; Shift+Enter starts a new line.
heart.board.help.move:
Move selects things and moves them. You can select cards, pins, strings, and brush strokes. A faint red outline shows what a press takes. The outline is dashed when the thing is public.

**Select and move**
- **Click** to select. **Ctrl+click** adds to the selection or removes from it.
- **Drag a box** to select several. The box also takes the strokes that it touches.
- **Drag** the selection to move it. Writing that lies on a note moves with the note.
- **Corner brackets** size the selection. **Corner arrows** turn it.

**Strings and pins**
- **Ctrl+drag a string** to pin a joint into it.
- **Ctrl+drag a pin** to start a new string from it.
- **Shift+drag a string or a pin** to break it at that point.
- **Alt+drag a string** to change its shape.
- **Drag the pin of a string onto another pin** to join the two.
- Near a pin or a string, a white dot shows what a press takes. A ring shows when the dot has caught it.

**The pieces of a card**
- Select a card to show handles on its pieces: its clipping, tape, pins, and writing. Its strokes show an outline under the pointer.
- **Click a piece** to select it alone. Then move, turn, or size it.
- **Drag the writing off a note** to make it writing on the sheet.
- **Drag writing onto a blank note** to make it the writing of the note.
- **Ctrl+drag a box** to select only what is on the card. The card stays selected.

**Lock**
- **Right-click** a card or a stroke to lock it or let it go. A padlock shows on what is locked.
- A locked card is frozen for everyone, you also. Nothing on it changes until you let it go. Strings still tie to it.

**Double-click** a place to open it, a note or writing to edit it, or a string to change its kind, name, and colour.
heart.board.help.reveal:
Reveal shows things to the players or hides them.

- **Click a place** to move it on one step: hidden, rumoured, then known. **Right-click** moves it back one step.
- **Click** a note, writing, a pin, or a string to show it or hide it.
- A string also shows every string that joins it end to end, up to a branch, with their name tags.
- A string to a hidden place stays hidden until you reveal the place.
heart.board.help.string:
String ties strings between cards or across the sheet. The String window sets the next string before you make it, and shows a short part of it as it will be.

**The String window**
- **Kind**: **No kind** (a white thread, its pins their own colour) to start, or a delve, a Vermissian line, or a path.
- **Paint**: any paint, or none.
- **Pin**: the pin at each end.
- **Pins in its colour**: the end pins take the colour of the string. This is on at the start.

**Make a string**
- **Click where it starts, then click where it ends.** You can also press and drag.
- On a card, the string ties at that point. Anywhere else, it hangs loose.
- **Hold Ctrl** to make one string after another, each from the end of the last.
- **Right-click** to stop a string that is not finished.

A new string is selected. **Double-click** it with Move to change its name, kind, colour, or the colour of its pins. When you delete a string, the pins that no other string holds go with it.
heart.board.help.string-player:
String ties your own strings. The String window sets your next string before you make it.

- **Paint**: the colour of the string, or none: a white thread.
- **Pin**: the pin at each end.
- **Pins in its colour**: the end pins take the colour of the string.

**Make a string**
- **Click where it starts, then click where it ends.** You can also press and drag. A string can start on a card or anywhere on the sheet.
- **Double-click** a string with Move to change its colour, the colour of its pins, or its name.
- **Delete** removes a selected string, and the pins that no other string holds.
heart.board.help.note:
Note pins a paper note to the board. The note window shows the note as the board will draw it.

- **Click the board** to make a note. **Click a note** to edit it.
- **Type** the writing. **Enter** saves. **Shift+Enter** starts a new line.
- **Bold**, **Italic**, **Underline**, and **Strike** apply to the selected writing and to what you type next. **Ctrl+B**, **Ctrl+I**, and **Ctrl+U** also work.
- **Align** applies to the whole note.
- A new note starts in **Soot**, the darkest paint, at Medium.
- **Hand**, **Paint**, **Brightness**, and **Tilt** set how the writing and the paper look.
- **Drag on the note** in the window to move its writing.
- **Text size**: Fit fills the note. Move the slider for smaller writing.
- **Paper**: the window picks one at the start. The dice picks another.
- **Public** lets everyone change the note.

A note can be blank. Save it with no writing, then add writing later, or drag writing from the sheet onto it. After you move, size, or turn the writing of a note, the writing keeps its size. Writing that nobody moved fills its note.
heart.board.help.write:
Write puts writing straight onto the sheet.

- **Click the sheet** to write. **Click writing** to edit it.
- **Drag writing onto a blank note** to make it the writing of the note.
- Writing that lies on a note shows on the note and moves with it.
heart.board.help.erase:
Erase removes brush strokes and nothing else. A ring under the pointer shows its size. As you drag, a red tint shows what it will take. The Erase window sets its size and its mode.

- **Parts** removes only the marker that the eraser passes over. The rest of each stroke stays.
- **Whole strokes** removes each stroke that the eraser touches.
- **Size** sets how large the eraser is. **Ctrl+scroll** also changes the size, and does not zoom.
- **Click** to erase one spot, or **drag** across the strokes.
- Erase never touches a locked stroke.

To remove pins, strings, and cards, select them with Move and press **Delete**. The brush window has the same eraser for **Shift+drag**.
heart.board.help.erase-player:
Erase removes brush strokes. A tinted area under the pointer shows what it will take. The Erase window sets its size and its mode.

- **Parts** removes only the marker that the eraser passes over. The rest of each stroke stays.
- **Whole strokes** removes each stroke that the eraser touches.
- **Size** sets how large the eraser is. **Ctrl+scroll** also changes the size, and does not zoom.
- **Click** to erase one spot, or **drag** across the strokes.

Erase takes only your own strokes, strokes on a note of yours, and public strokes. It never takes a locked stroke.
heart.board.help.pin:
Pin puts pins into cards or onto the board. The Pin window shows every pin, and the selected pin large.

- **Pick a pin** in the window. The pointer shows the pin where a click puts it.
- **Pick a paint** in the window to colour the pin. **Its own colour** leaves it as it is.
- **Click** to put it in. On a card, the pin goes into the card. Anywhere else, it sits loose on the board.
- With Move, **drag a pin** onto a card or off it.
heart.board.help.mark:
The brush paints on the sheet, under everything pinned to it, or on a card. A stroke that starts on a card stays on that card. The brush never paints on a locked card.

**The brush window**
- **Pen**, **Brush**, or **Wash** is the nib: a crisp ink line, the ink brush, or a see-through watercolour tint for woods, water, and fire. Each keeps its own width and opacity: the pen 3 and solid, the brush 8 at 85%, the wash broad and faint, a background under what is drawn over it.
- **Paints**, **Brightness**, **Width**, and **Opacity** set the next stroke. At 100% a stroke covers what is under it.
- If strokes are selected with Move, a change here changes all of them. **Clear** lets go of them.
- **Rub out (Shift+drag)** sets the size and mode of the eraser for **Shift+drag**. Hold **Shift** to see it under the pointer; **Shift+Ctrl+scroll** sizes it.
- **Double-click its head** to show only the paints, then only the head.
- **Doodles** opens the doodles window.
- **Reset all brushes** removes every stroke. **Ctrl+Z** brings them back.
- The **x** closes the window. If the doodles window is open, it stays open, with the brush in hand.

**Shift+drag** erases, the same as the Erase tool.
heart.board.help.inspect-player:
Look is for looking at the board.

- **Click** a known place to open it. You see its sheet if you have permission, and its picture if you do not.
- Rumoured places show a name with a question mark. They do not open.
- **Click and hold** to ping that spot for everyone.
heart.board.help.move-player:
Move selects your own notes, writing, strings, pins, and brush strokes, and public ones. A faint red outline shows what you can change. The outline is dashed when the thing is public, and shows a padlock when the thing is locked.

**Select and move**
- **Click** to select. **Ctrl+click** adds to the selection or removes from it.
- **Drag a box** to select several. The box also takes the strokes that it touches.
- **Drag** the selection to move it. Writing that lies on a note moves with the note.
- **Drag the corner square** to size the selection, and **drag the circle** to turn it. **Shift+wheel** also sizes, and **Ctrl+wheel** also turns.
- A single note stretches to any shape. **Shift+drag** the corner to keep its shape.

**The pieces of a note**
- Select one note to show white dots on its pieces: its writing, its pin, and a web. Its strokes show an outline.
- **Drag a piece** to move it on the note.
- **Drag the writing off the note** to make it writing on the sheet.
- **Drag writing onto a blank note** to make it the writing of the note.
- **Ctrl+drag a box** to select only what is on the note.

**Lock**
- **Right-click** a note, writing, or a stroke to lock it. **Right-click** again to let it go.
- Nobody can change a locked note until somebody lets it go. Anyone can lock or free a public note.

**Double-click** a note or writing to edit it, or a string to change its colour and name.
heart.board.help.note-player:
Note pins up a note in your own handwriting.

- **Click the board** to make a note. Your first note asks you to pick a hand. That hand stays yours for the whole campaign.
- **Click** a note of yours, or a public one, to edit it.
- **Type** the writing. **Enter** saves. **Shift+Enter** starts a new line.
- **Bold**, **Italic**, **Underline**, and **Strike** apply to the selected writing and to what you type next. **Ctrl+B**, **Ctrl+I**, and **Ctrl+U** also work.
- A new note starts in **Soot**, the darkest paint.
- **Drag on the note** in the window to move its writing.
- **Text size**: Fit fills the note. Move the slider for smaller writing.
- **Public** lets everyone change the note.

A note can be blank. Add writing later, or drag writing from the sheet onto it. After you move, size, or turn the writing of a note, the writing keeps its size.
heart.board.help.write-player:
Write puts writing straight onto the sheet, in your handwriting.

- **Click the sheet** to write. **Click** your writing, or public writing, to edit it.
- **Drag writing onto a blank note** to make it the writing of the note.
- Writing that lies on a note shows on the note and moves with it.
heart.board.help.mark-player:
The brush paints on the sheet or on a card. A stroke that starts on a card moves with the card. The brush never paints on a locked card.

**The brush window**
- **Pen**, **Brush**, or **Wash** is the nib: a crisp ink line, the ink brush, or a see-through watercolour tint for woods, water, and fire. Each keeps its own width and opacity: the pen 3 and solid, the brush 8 at 85%, the wash broad and faint, a background under what is drawn over it.
- **Paints**, **Brightness**, **Width**, and **Opacity** set the next stroke. At 100% a stroke covers what is under it.
- If strokes are selected with Move, a change here changes all of them. **Clear** lets go of them.
- **Rub out (Shift+drag)** sets the size and mode of the eraser for **Shift+drag**. Hold **Shift** to see it under the pointer; **Shift+Ctrl+scroll** sizes it.
- **Double-click its head** to show only the paints, then only the head.
- **Doodles** opens the doodles window.
- The **x** closes the window. If the doodles window is open, it stays open, with the brush in hand.

**Shift+drag** erases your own strokes, the same as the Erase tool.
heart.board.help.intro-player:
What you make is yours. Only you and the GM can change it, until you make it public. Anyone can change, move, or remove a public thing.

Everyone sees each mark when it lands. Point at a button to see its name. Rest the pointer on a note or a string to see whose it is.
heart.board.help.turn: On the board's own toolbar: puts the toolbar up the left side of the screen, or along the top.
heart.board.help.undo:
Each person undoes only their own edits, never the edits of another person.

- **Ctrl+Z** undoes your last edit on the board.
- **Ctrl+Y** or **Ctrl+Shift+Z** does it again.
- The arrows on the toolbar do the same.
heart.board.help.delete:
**Delete** or **Backspace** removes the selection.

- Selected pins, strings, and brush strokes go at once. A locked stroke never goes.
- Selected cards go only after you agree. They go to File, Removed cards. A locked card never goes.
- A piece of a card that is selected alone goes by itself: a strip of tape, a pin through its clipping, or the writing of a note. The note stays, blank. **Ctrl+Z** puts it back.
- The picture of a place never goes.
heart.board.help.delete-player:
**Delete** or **Backspace** removes the selection.

- Your selected strings, pins, and brush strokes go at once, and public ones. A locked stroke never goes.
- Your selected notes and writing, and public ones, go after you agree. The GM keeps them in Removed cards, and **Ctrl+Z** puts them back.
- A note does not go if it is locked, or if strings or pins of another person are on it.
- A piece of a note that is selected alone goes by itself: its writing or a web. **Ctrl+Z** puts it back.
heart.board.help.preview: Shows the board as the players see it, with their tools. Click the button again to come back.
heart.board.help.file:
The File menu holds the tools for the whole board. Each tile has a short name. Point at a tile to see its full name.

- **Save Render**: downloads the whole map, as you see it, at full resolution: **Balanced** (a WebP, balanced between quality and size) or **Quality** (a lossless PNG, unlimited quality).
- **Statistics**: what is on the board, what everyone is doing, and how this computer keeps up. It updates every second while it is open.
- **Quality**: how finely this computer paints the board, in one click. It is the same as Board detail in Configure Settings.
- **New place**: makes a place at the table, with a name and a picture if you want. It is a landmark actor in the Board places folder, and its card follows its name. It goes in hidden or known, at the middle of the view or where you click next.
- **Reshuffle**, also **Shift+R**: puts the selected cards together again: paper, clipping, tape and pins, tilt, and grime.
- **Sheet size**: adds or removes pages on any side. It never removes a page with something on it.
- **Map layers** (on a board with a baked map): each overlay shown or hidden, each roof on or lifted, and how far players see NPCs.
- **Show my moves**: everyone sees what you paint, drag, or hold as you do it. It is on at the start. Turn it off for quiet preparation.
- **Removed cards**: the cards that were taken off, to put back.
- **Earlier boards**: copies that this browser kept, to put one back.
- **Download**: saves the board as a .json file, named for the scene and the day.
- **Export** and **Import**: the board as text for the map editor, and a board pasted from it or loaded from a file. The board that an import replaces becomes the backup.
- **Backup**: swaps in the board from before the last import.
- **Reload look**: reads the art of the map again after the editor exports it.

**Ctrl+Z** takes back a reshuffle or a change of sheet size. The Board tab of the scene's settings sets the style, the background, and the size of the board.
heart.board.help.file-player:
- **Save Render** downloads the whole map, as you see it, at full resolution: **Balanced** (a WebP, balanced between quality and size) or **Quality** (a lossless PNG, unlimited quality).
- **Statistics** shows what is on the board, what everyone is doing, and how your computer keeps up. It updates every second while it is open.
- **Quality** sets how finely your computer paints the board, in one click. Lower it if the map is slow for you.
heart.board.help.alone: On the brush window: shows only the brush strokes, until you put the brush down.
heart.board.help.doodles:
Doodles are small drawings that the brush lays down with one click. **Doodles** on the brush window opens or closes the doodles window.

- **Places**, **Signs**, and **Yours** are its tabs: places to mark on the map, signs to set beside them, and the drawings you kept. Places and signs are the GM's; a player sees only their own.
- **Pick a doodle**, then **click** where it goes. On a card, it stays on the card. The pointer shows it as it will be.
- **Size** and **Turn** set it. **Shift+wheel** and **Ctrl+wheel** also set it. **Mirror**, or **R**, flips it across its upright axis; its turn stays.
- **Pick strokes** turns picking on and off, the brush still in hand: drag a box round strokes to select them, drag again to start over, **Ctrl+drag** to add more, and **Ctrl+click** a stroke to take or let go of it. A **right-click** stops, nothing selected.
- **Save the selected strokes** keeps them (or strokes selected with Move) as a doodle of your own, in their own paints, on every map. **Clear** lets go of them.
- **Right-click** one of your doodles to forget it.
- **Escape** puts the doodle down.
- The window that you pressed last is in hand: the brush or the doodle.

**The doodles window**
- It opens beside the brush window, with its top bar level and the same height.
- Let it go next to any side of the brush window and it snaps there. It matches the height on a side, or the width above or below.
- Move it anywhere else and it stays there. Its link button snaps it back, and its **x** closes it.
heart.board.help.keys:
- **PageUp** and **PageDown** move the selected cards one layer up or down.
- **Enter** removes a selected pin and keeps the string: a joint goes, or two strings that meet end to end become one.
- **Escape** puts a doodle down.
- **Ctrl+wheel** turns the selection, and **Shift+wheel** sizes it. With a doodle in hand, they turn and size the doodle. With Erase in hand, **Ctrl+wheel** sizes the eraser; with the brush, **Shift+Ctrl+wheel** sizes its eraser.
- The **wheel** alone zooms.
- **Shift+P** makes the selection public, or gives it back to its maker. **Shift+right-click** does the same for what is under the pointer.
- **Shift+R** puts the selected cards together again.
- **Ctrl+B**, **Ctrl+I**, and **Ctrl+U** set bold, italic, and underline in the note window.
- **Click the tool in hand again** to put it down and go to Look.
heart.board.help.keys-player:
- **Ctrl+wheel** turns the selected notes or writing, and **Shift+wheel** sizes them. With a doodle in hand, they turn and size the doodle. With Erase in hand, **Ctrl+wheel** sizes the eraser; with the brush, **Shift+Ctrl+wheel** sizes its eraser.
- The **wheel** alone zooms.
- **Shift+P** makes what you selected public, or yours again. **Shift+right-click** does the same for what is under the pointer.
- **Enter** removes a selected pin of yours and keeps the string: a joint goes, or two strings that meet end to end become one.
- **Escape** puts a doodle down.
- **Ctrl+B**, **Ctrl+I**, and **Ctrl+U** set bold, italic, and underline in the note window.
- **Click the tool in hand again** to put it down and go to Look.
heart.board.note-enter-drag: Enter writes it; Shift+Enter starts a new line. Drag on the note to move its writing.
heart.board.text-size-hint: Fit: as large as fits on the note. Slide left for smaller writing.

What anyone makes is theirs until they make it public. Anyone can change, move, or remove a public note, writing, string, or pin, and the pieces on it. Only its maker and the GM can make it public, or theirs again.

- **Select it and press the people button**, or press **Shift+P**.
- **Shift+right-click** it.
- **Tick Public** in its window.
- Do it again to make it theirs again.
- Rest the pointer on a note or a string to see whose it is.
